Mossy Forest with WGCNA Module Detection

Source: R/mf_fit.R
wmf.Rd

Runs a Weighted Gene Co expression Network Analysis (WGCNA) to derive module membership, then passes the result to mf.

Usage

wmf(
  X,
  y,
  WGCNA_params = WGCNA_control(power = 6),
  screen_params = screen_control(),
  select_params = select_control(),
  final_ntree = 500L,
  nodesize = NULL,
  num_processors = 1L,
  max_modsize = 5000L,
  verbose = 1L,
  seed = as.integer(Sys.time()),
  backend = "python",
  r_shap = "permutation",
  compute_interactions = TRUE
)

Arguments

X

A data frame where each column is a feature.

y

Response vector (numeric for regression, factor for classification).

WGCNA_params

WGCNA parameters. See WGCNA_control.

screen_params

Screening parameters. See screen_control.

select_params

Selection parameters. See select_control.

final_ntree

Number of trees in the final random forest. Default 500.

nodesize

Minimum terminal node size. Defaults to 1 for classification and 5 for regression.

num_processors

Number of parallel threads for random forests. Default 1.

max_modsize

Maximum module size before blockwise pre reduction is applied (Python backend only). Default 5000.

verbose

Verbose level. 0 = silent; 1 = progress messages; 2 = detailed output. Default 1.

seed

Integer random seed for reproducibility. Defaults to current system time.

backend

Computation backend. "python" (default) uses a Python scikit-learn / SHAP engine via reticulate and provides exact TreeSHAP values plus an interaction matrix. "R" uses a R ranger implementation, no Python installation required. Choose the final importance method with r_shap.

r_shap

Final SHAP / importance method used when backend = "R". Ignored for the Python backend. One of:

"permutation"

Ranger permutation variable importance (default). No extra packages needed. Returns a scalar VIM per feature; per observation SHAP values and SHAP based plots are unavailable.

"treeshap"

Exact TreeSHAP values via the R treeshap package. Requires treeshap. Also computes a \(p \times p\) interaction matrix, enabling detect_interaction() and plot_potential_interactions().

compute_interactions

Logical. If TRUE (default), the TreeSHAP interaction matrix is computed by the Python backend and by the pure R backend with r_shap = "treeshap". Set FALSE to skip it (faster); detect_interaction() and plot_potential_interactions() then have nothing to use. It has no effect with r_shap = "permutation", which never computes interactions.

Value

An object of class mossy_forest with an additional $WGCNA_object slot containing the raw WGCNA output.

References

Zhang, B., & Horvath, S. (2005). A general framework for weighted gene co expression network analysis. Statistical Applications in Genetics and Molecular Biology, 4(1), Article 17.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Two blocks of correlated features; WGCNA finds the modules
set.seed(1)
n <- 30
z1 <- rnorm(n); z2 <- rnorm(n)
block <- function(k, zz) as.data.frame(replicate(k, zz + rnorm(n, sd = 0.4)))
X <- cbind(block(10, z1), block(10, z2))
colnames(X) <- paste0("g", seq_len(ncol(X)))
y <- z1 - z2 + rnorm(n, sd = 0.3)
fit <- wmf(X, y, WGCNA_params = WGCNA_control(power = 6, min_features = 6),
           screen_params = screen_control(min_ntree = 30),
           select_params = select_control(n_reps = 3, min_ntree = 30),
           final_ntree = 30, backend = "R", verbose = 0, seed = 1)
table(fit$WGCNA_object$colors)
#> 
#>      blue turquoise 
#>        10        10 
# }
